Definition: properly, to cover with pieces; i.e. (by implication) to spot or variegate (as tapestry)
BiblicalUsage: Jacob says, I will pass through all thy flock today, removing every speckled and spotted sheep, and every brown among the lambs. Laban removes the ringstraked and spotted goats that very day. And the Gibeonites come to Joshua with old sacks, old and rent wineskins, and old shoes clouted upon their feet, and the word is to cover with pieces, to spot and variegate: speckled flocks and patched shoes.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe the speckled sheep are the hinge of Jacob's story: the spotted ones were his wages, and God gave them to him, and the patched shoes of the Gibeonites are the other side — a deception stitched together.
